identity.fantasy: A Rexxar-like beast fighter who fights shoulder to shoulder with a tameable companion, chaining claws, totems, boons, and shared frenzies.
identity.one_line: A Rexxar-like beast fighter with a tameable companion. Rylak's Bite, Wildclaw, Primal Shred, Totemic Smash, and animal Boons coordinate player and pet attacks. It is a forgiving leveler because the pet can hold enemies and the base class has self-healing.

mechanics.core_loop: Let the companion hold or pressure the target, use Rylak's Bite and melee attacks to drive pet synergy, weave Totemic Smash and Primal Shred, maintain bleeds and rage, then align Savage Frenzy, Bestial Wrath, or late Totem Warrior and Rexxar payoffs with durable targets.

modes.name: Throat Clamp
modes.structural_description: Command your pet to dash forward a short distance towards your target, interrupting spellcasting and preventing any spell in that school from being cast for 3 seconds.

modes.name: Son of Ursoc
modes.structural_description: Your Savage Frenzy now transforms you into a feast beast, freeing you of all movement impairing effects.In addition, increases the effectiveness of Savage Frenzy by 50%, and reduces its cooldown by -60 sec.

mechanics.single_target: Coordinate Rylak's Bite, Primal Shred, pet attacks, bleeds, and shared frenzy windows for sustained melee pressure.
mechanics.aoe: Totemic Smash, Pulverize, Tremors, Earthshaker, and pet cleave support dungeon packs; a current Build Hub build is specifically AoE-focused.
mechanics.movement_and_target_switching: The pet maintains pressure while the player moves, and Boulder Dash or Rush of the Hunt help reconnect or escape.
mechanics.defense_and_control: Plate armor, rage-based healing, pet tanking, Throat Clamp, Boulder Dash, and boons make it one of the more forgiving non-tank levelers.
mechanics.group_utility: Totems, boons, pet control, and Primalist group tools add utility without replacing the damage role.

failure_modes.text: Allowing the pet to lose contact or desynchronizing shared frenzy and boon windows lowers both sides of the paired damage engine.
Movement or a target swap can interrupt the intended payoff: the pet maintains pressure while the player moves, and boulder dash or rush of the hunt help reconnect or escape.

Spending recovery or control too early leaves less protection for the next pressure event: plate armor, rage-based healing, pet tanking, throat clamp, boulder dash, and boons make it one of the more forgiving non-tank levelers.

enjoy_if.text: You want a durable Rexxar-style melee hunter with a meaningful tameable companion.

You enjoy the spec's core cadence: let the companion hold or pressure the target, use rylak's bite and melee attacks to drive pet synergy, weave totemic smash and primal shred, maintain bleeds and rage, then align savage frenzy, bestial wrath, or late totem warrior and rexxar payoffs with durable targets.

avoid_if.text: You dislike pet dependence or want a purely personal melee rotation.
You dislike the positioning or swap constraint that the pet maintains pressure while the player moves, and boulder dash or rush of the hunt help reconnect or escape.

praise.theme: Players repeatedly call Wildwalker smooth, forgiving, durable, and strong for solo leveling because the pet tanks and healing costs Rage rather than mana.

frustrations.theme: Some players find the higher-level Enhancement-like proc cadence APM intensive or do not gel with the pet-brawler loop.

gaps: No current detailed level-60 single-target guide.
Pet species and boon optimization are not compared.

claims.text: Recent players describe Wildwalker as a smooth, forgiving Rexxar-like leveler: the pet tanks, plate armor reduces pressure, healing costs Rage rather than mana, and Boulder Dash provides a strong escape. Higher-level reports compare it to an APM-intensive Enhancement Shaman with a pet.
claims.notes: Community label Wildwalker maps to current dataset name Primal.

claims.text: The July DPS compilation reports Wildwalker at 3,997, and the August Mythic inventory lists 101 Wildwalker records.
claims.notes: Community label Wildwalker maps to current dataset name Primal; performance methodology is incomplete.

claims.text: Primal's output is split between player and companion, so pet downtime or mismatched shared frenzy and boon windows reduce the total engine even when the player's buttons continue normally.
claims.notes: Pet share is not quantified.

claims.text: Current players describe Primal as an easy PvE leveler whose companion tanks, self-healing stabilizes pulls, and AoE works in dungeons, while battleground performance is reported weaker.
claims.notes: Manually reviewed on 2026-08-06; anecdotal evidence is not treated as a power ranking.
